contract_profiles.exit_contract: Exit zero only when every checked invariant holds; malformed input, missing required input, and semantic drift are failures.
contract_profiles.ordering: Read and compare inputs deterministically; preserve validation order where it controls the first diagnostic.
contract_profiles.diagnostics: Actionable diagnostics go to stderr and identify the rejected file, field, fixture, or invariant.
contract_profiles.schema: Preserve every accepted checked-in JSON, TSV, source, header, and text contract byte-for-byte unless a separately reviewed schema version changes.
contract_profiles.network: Offline. Any required repository, corpus, SDK, or fixture must already be present.

contract_profiles.exit_contract: Exit zero only after complete deterministic output; reject malformed or incomplete inputs and never accept a partial artifact.
contract_profiles.ordering: Canonical sorting, stable formatting, and existing replacement order are part of the output contract.
contract_profiles.diagnostics: Parse and generation failures identify the source input and rejected record; diagnostics never contaminate stdout artifacts.
contract_profiles.schema: Generated Zig, JSON, Markdown, TSV, or binary bytes remain compatible with the checked consumer and checked artifact.
contract_profiles.network: Offline. Operator-provided inputs must exist before generation.

contract_profiles.exit_contract: Exit zero only after every requested artifact is fetched, pinned or checksum-verified, and completely materialized.
contract_profiles.ordering: Acquire, verify, then generate or extract; an unverified byte must never reach a checked artifact.
contract_profiles.diagnostics: Network, checksum, archive, and conversion failures name the URL, expected identity, and failed phase.
contract_profiles.schema: Acquired inputs and generated outputs retain their pinned corpus or standards-data version contract.
contract_profiles.network: Network is allowed only as an explicit operator action and is governed by the pinned-acquisition boundary in #462.

contract_profiles.exit_contract: Exit zero only for complete samples that pass identity, pairing, statistics, and publication validation.
contract_profiles.ordering: Preserve warmup/sample order, A/B balancing, aggregation order, and exact-parent identity checks.
contract_profiles.diagnostics: Failures name the benchmark, engine, sample, statistic, identity, or evidence field that violated the contract.
contract_profiles.schema: Versioned raw TSV/JSON and rendered Markdown/README regions retain their current columns, units, metadata, and statistics.
contract_profiles.network: Offline after engines and checked evidence are present; publication never fetches data.

contract_profiles.exit_contract: Exit nonzero for runner failure, unexpected corpus outcome, timeout, malformed inventory, or denominator drift.
contract_profiles.ordering: Preserve corpus discovery order, sharding, timeout/reaping rules, result classification, and deterministic summaries.
contract_profiles.diagnostics: Failures retain case paths, modes, commands, captured output, and summary counts on the established streams.
contract_profiles.schema: Corpus inventories, logs, allowlists, and summary JSON keep their versioned fields and disposition vocabulary.
contract_profiles.network: Offline. Corpora and runner binaries must already be present.

contract_profiles.exit_contract: Exit zero only when all positive, malformed-input, and deliberate failure-path assertions pass.
contract_profiles.ordering: Test discovery and assertion behavior remain deterministic.
contract_profiles.diagnostics: Failed assertions identify the test and preserve compared values or captured failure text.
contract_profiles.schema: No artifact schema; fixtures encode compatibility contracts for a retained tool or a future Home-executed TypeScript implementation.

contract_profiles.exit_contract: Exit zero only when the exact required tool or source is available and verified; partial setup is failure.
contract_profiles.ordering: Resolve existing owned/local state first, then acquire, verify, and install in that order.
contract_profiles.diagnostics: Failures name the missing tool, platform, URL or repository identity, expected pin, and failed setup phase.
contract_profiles.schema: Installed tool identity, archive layout, and invocation contract stay compatible with CI callers.
contract_profiles.network: Network is restricted to explicit CI or operator bootstrap and exact identities must be enforced.

contract_profiles.exit_contract: Exit zero only after validating scope and completing the requested report or recoverable maintenance action.
contract_profiles.ordering: Inspect and validate targets before mutation; dry-run/report modes never mutate.
contract_profiles.diagnostics: Diagnostics show resolved targets and refuse any path outside the narrow declared scope.
contract_profiles.schema: Human-readable report and CLI flags remain compatible with documented operator commands.
